[
  {"step":1,"file":"repo-vul/src-vul/libssh/src/messages.c","function":"ssh_packet_channel_open","line":1067,"var":"type_c","code":"rc = ssh_buffer_unpack(packet, \"s\", &type_c);","note":"Attacker-controlled channel-open type string is unpacked from the SSH packet into a heap-allocated C string."},
  {"step":2,"file":"repo-vul/src-vul/libssh/src/messages.c","function":"ssh_packet_channel_open","line":1074,"var":"type_c","code":"SSH_LOG(..., \"Clients wants to open a %s channel\", type_c);","note":"The unpacked string is consumed to steer later parsing and request dispatch."},
  {"step":3,"file":"repo-vul/src-vul/libssh/src/messages.c","function":"ssh_packet_channel_open","line":1080,"var":"msg->channel_request_open.sender/window/packet_size","code":"ssh_buffer_unpack(packet, \"ddd\", ...);","note":"The packet cursor advances through additional attacker-controlled fields before the request-specific branch."},
  {"step":4,"file":"repo-vul/src-vul/libssh/src/messages.c","function":"ssh_packet_channel_open","line":1085,"var":"session->session_state","code":"if (session->session_state != SSH_SESSION_STATE_AUTHENTICATED) goto error;","note":"The code only continues for authenticated sessions, so the malformed packet must reach this parser in an authenticated context."},
  {"step":5,"file":"repo-vul/src-vul/libssh/src/messages.c","function":"ssh_packet_channel_open","line":1089,"var":"strcmp(type_c, \"session\")","code":"if (strcmp(type_c,\"session\") == 0) { ... goto end; }","note":"A non-session type keeps execution in the request-dispatch logic instead of taking the safe early exit."},
  {"step":6,"file":"repo-vul/src-vul/libssh/src/messages.c","function":"ssh_packet_channel_open","line":1094,"var":"strcmp(type_c, \"direct-tcpip\")","code":"if (strcmp(type_c,\"direct-tcpip\") == 0) { rc = ssh_buffer_unpack(packet, \"sdsd\", ...); }","note":"The direct-tcpip branch performs further unpacking of attacker-controlled strings and integers from the same packet buffer."},
  {"step":7,"file":"repo-vul/src-vul/libssh/src/buffer.c","function":"ssh_buffer_unpack_va","line":1149,"var":"*o.cstring","code":"*o.cstring = NULL;","note":"For format 's', the destination pointer is cleared before length validation and allocation."},
  {"step":8,"file":"repo-vul/src-vul/libssh/src/buffer.c","function":"ssh_buffer_unpack_va","line":1150,"var":"u32len","code":"rc = ssh_buffer_get_u32(buffer, &u32len);","note":"The next four bytes from the attacker-controlled buffer are interpreted as the string length."},
  {"step":9,"file":"repo-vul/src-vul/libssh/src/buffer.c","function":"ssh_buffer_unpack_va","line":1155,"var":"len","code":"len = ntohl(u32len);","note":"The raw length is converted to host order and becomes the size used for bounds checks and allocation."},
  {"step":10,"file":"repo-vul/src-vul/libssh/src/buffer.c","function":"ssh_buffer_unpack_va","line":1156,"var":"len","code":"if (len > max_len - 1) { rc = SSH_ERROR; break; }","note":"The parser rejects oversized strings, so the exploit hypothesis is that a crafted packet must satisfy this check while still driving the vulnerable sink elsewhere."},
  {"step":11,"file":"repo-vul/src-vul/libssh/src/buffer.c","function":"ssh_buffer_unpack_va","line":1161,"var":"buffer","code":"rc = ssh_buffer_validate_length(buffer, len);","note":"The buffer length is validated before copying the string payload out of the packet."},
  {"step":12,"file":"repo-vul/src-vul/libssh/src/buffer.c","function":"ssh_buffer_unpack_va","line":1166,"var":"*o.cstring","code":"*o.cstring = malloc(len + 1);","note":"A heap buffer is allocated for the unpacked string, making later consumers depend on the attacker-chosen length and contents."},
  {"step":13,"file":"repo-vul/src-vul/libssh/src/buffer.c","function":"ssh_buffer_unpack_va","line":1171,"var":"*o.cstring","code":"rlen = ssh_buffer_get_data(buffer, *o.cstring, len);","note":"The attacker-controlled bytes are copied into the newly allocated destination."},
  {"step":14,"file":"repo-vul/src-vul/libssh/src/buffer.c","function":"ssh_buffer_unpack_va","line":1177,"var":"(*o.cstring)[len]","code":"(*o.cstring)[len] = '\\0';","note":"The unpacked string is NUL-terminated and then returned to the caller for subsequent use."}
]
